subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact TypeScript module for a cyberpunk riot-control interceptor vehicle—an armored truck with a water cannon turret, neon light bars, and corporate yellow/black and cyan/magenta styling, built using box primitives and helper functions.

Working out dimensions: a wheelbase roughly 5.8m long and 2.3m wide, wheel radius 0.5 positioned to touch the floor, and a chassis joint height around 0.7m. I'm designing the hull using paneled paint textures and planning custom SVG decals for an invented corporate logo, light bar glow, warning chevrons, a license plate, and a HUD visor, then laying out the body sections front to back starting with the lower hull box and cab frustum.

Now I'm sketching the cab windscreen as a sloped glass box, the hood as a tapered frustum, and the armored rear compartment, then adding a roof turret with yaw/pitch joints, a glowing water cannon nozzle, and side-mounted water tank cylinders.

I'm also planning the push bar bumper with chevron texture, alternating neon light bars with glow effects along the roof and rockers, glowing headlight slits, mesh window cages for the cab, seam and door handle details, and roof-mounted speaker horns.

Then I'm detailing the side shields with decals, exhaust stacks, glowing tail lights, rear door chevrons, wheels with tread blocks and glowing magenta rim rings, fender arches, and mud flaps. For the wheel rigging I'm setting cylinder rotation along the X axis with hub joints pointing outward, deciding to keep the front wheel hinge simple and parented directly to the chassis rather than adding separate steering joints.

Adding wheel treads and lug nuts...

Now I'm defining the color palette as a dark navy-black body with yellow, cyan, and magenta accents, plus glass tones. For the hull finish I'm thinking through using a panelled paint texture with seams for riveted detail.

For the hull paint, I'm blending a dark base with grime wear near the bottom, then applying it through the panelled texture generator with rivets. I'm also setting up a decal helper to place textures like a corporate hexagon logo onto side faces of the hull.

I'm planning out the full texture set: chevron stripes for the bumper, a segmented glowing lightbar strip, a warning label with unit number, a plate, a scanline HUD visor for the windscreen, a water tank wave icon, and a tail light. For the windscreen I'm using a tilted box part with the scanline texture applied.

Now I'm working out the geometry for the cab's sloped windscreen, computing the normal direction and positioning so the glass angles back correctly, splitting the cab into a lower box for the dash/hood and an upper frustum for the greenhouse section.

I'll stack the hood, cab, and greenhouse boxes with proper offsets, then add a roof slab, pillars in body color, dark glass panels, and a sloped windscreen plane on top to tie the cab structure together.

Now I'm adding the roof cage rods over the side windows, then setting up the turret mount on the rear compartment roof with yaw and pitch hinge joints, followed by the barrel rod geometry.

I'm checking clearances: making sure the barrel sits high enough over the cab roof and light bar without clipping, nudging the turret position and barrel length to keep the gap between roof-mounted parts and the barrel's underside.

Now I'm designing the water cannon itself—a tube with a flared nozzle, glowing cyan water ring at the tip, ribbed details, and a hose sweeping from the tank to the turret. I'm splitting the turret into yaw components (drum, cheek plates, camera) and pitch components (barrel, breech, rings, nozzle, sight scope with a glowing lens, top rail), and placing twin horizontal tanks along the outer sides of the rear compartment.

I'm reconsidering tank placement since the side position makes them too wide relative to the hull and wheels, so I'm trying mounting them atop the rear box instead, checking clearances against the turret drum position and sketching where a water decal plane would sit on each tank's outer face.

Since a flat decal can't properly conform to a cylinder's curved surface, I'm scrapping that idea and going with painted bands in contrasting colors instead, plus a separate flat WATER panel mounted on the rear box side. I also want to add thin magenta underglow strips along the rockers beneath the chassis.

Now I'm designing the front bumper with chevron texturing and angled prongs, a light bar, and push-bar uprights, then moving to the rear with chevron doors, vertical glowing red tail light bars, a plate, dual exhausts, and a rear step. For the roof, I'm planning a light bar housing with alternating cyan/magenta glow segments, forward-facing horn speaker cones on the cab roof, a whip antenna, and a camera dome.

Side doors get thin dark seam outlines, a raised panel, handle, hinge cylinders, and a rigging joint for door articulation. I'm also adding side logo decals, a number plate, mirror stalks, and dark wheel arch boxes above the wheels.

Checking wheel-hull geometry, I notice the wheels slightly intrude into the hull volume, so I'm adding fender flares as body-colored caps over each wheel and widening the hull slightly to reduce the overlap for a cleaner fit.

Working out the hood's tapering box geometry, figuring the width/height sizes at each end and how the vertical axis aligns so the hood blends into the cab height around y 1.15-1.5.

Now I'm planning the grille assembly: a dark housing box with horizontal rod details, plus glowing headlight slits positioned on the front fascia at roughly x ±0.7, y 1.3.

Checking overall proportions next — total length around 5.9 units, height to 3.0 with the turret, front and rear wheel positions at z 1.9 and -1.7. Then I'm setting up a helper function to place parts relative to the chassis bone, simplifying how each box geometry gets attached.

Now I'm writing geometry helpers for boxes and cylinders, plus a glow wrapper and a decal helper for applying textures to planes. For paint, I'm layering a grimy mud-mix material over a panelled base using noise-driven color blending, importing the shading utilities from the SDK and the clockwork/glow kits. Finally I'm setting up the rig, marking the chassis as the spine and defining hinge-role joints for the wheels.

Still working through the wheel setup, defining hub positions and steering joints for the front wheels versus direct chassis mounts for the rear, then spinning joints driving each wheel bone. I'm sizing the tyre cylinder with enough segments that its flat facets stay close enough to the floor contact point without visible gaps.

For the tread blocks, I'm placing boxes around the tyre radius, but realize the carcass-plus-block thickness pushes the true wheel radius out further than expected, so I need to bump the hub height up to around 0.53 to keep the blocks from sinking below the ground plane.

Checking clearances, I see the flare cap bottom and wheel top nearly collide, so I'm raising the flare cap to 1.15 to fix it. Then for orienting each tread block around the wheel's circumference, I work out that rotating about the X-axis by the block's angular position correctly aligns its radial direction with the circle's tangent, matching the sampling formula.

Now I'm laying out the rim details: the steel rim cylinder, a glowing magenta neon ring torus, a hub cap, six lug nuts spaced radially, and deciding to skip visible sidewall text and hide the brake disc since it won't be seen. I'm also placing rear mud flaps behind each wheel, working out their position relative to the rear fender flare and hull end.

Next I'm sketching the texture SVGs: a logo graphic with a yellow hexagon outline, "VS" and "VANTAGE" text in a bold condensed font, plus bar accents, and a chevron pattern texture made of repeating black parallelograms over a yellow background generated via a loop.

Positioning the cab and rear box panels with logo and label depths set, then adding glowing red tail light boxes and rear door panels with seams and handles.

Now I'm placing the chevron decal strip along the bottom, rear box roof details like vents, tanks, and antenna, plus the cab's roof light bar housing and its front-facing texture strip.

Adding neon accents on sides and hood, plus siren pods at the ends of the light bar, then working through the geometry for the front bumper plow extrusion.

I'm adding push-bar uprights as rods running from the bumper up to the hood front at x ±0.8, plus a top crossbar, skipping the extra spike prongs for now. Then I'm positioning headlights above the bumper top at y 1.35, checking they clear the plow geometry against the hood front face.

Placing glow boxes for the headlights and a dark grille box between them with connecting rods. I'm also planning a windscreen wire-guard mesh, slanted vertical rods spaced across the windscreen plane, plus roof extras like a camera dome, wipers, cab step, and door handle.

Writing hose and turret code...

Still building the barrel geometry...

Still working out the cab greenhouse structure and cage rods...

Adding rib bands and trim stripes to the rear box, then estimating total wheel part counts, and defining paint materials with grime noise for the hull and a weathered yellow paint with scratch wear for the bumper.

For the tank I'm setting up a banded paint alternating steel gray and cyan stripes along its length, then checking that glow effects applied to textured parts still work with flat colors or plain white planes.

Now I'm defining my color palette (cyan, magenta, yellow, red, dark, steel, glass tones) and sketching out side mirrors with a stalk rod and glass-faced box, plus starting on the rear exhaust stack pipes positioned at the rear corners.

Adding exhaust pipe geometry...

Still placing extruded panels...

Still writing assembly code...
